chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu al-Ward, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who killed a slave by mistake. He said: "His value is due from him, and his value is not to exceed ten thousand dirhams."

I said: "Who appraises him when he is dead?" He said: "If his master has witnesses that his value on the day he killed him was such-and-such, then his killer is charged accordingly. If his master has no witnesses, then the valuation rests with the one who killed him together with his oath: he swears four times by Allah that he had no value greater than what I assessed for him. If he refuses to swear and returns the oath to the master, the master is given what he swore to, and his value is not to exceed ten thousand dirhams."

He said: "If the slave was a believer and he killed him intentionally, he must pay his value, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, feed sixty needy persons, and repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ رَقَبَةً: he must free a slave as expiation
key_terms.تَابَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: he must repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty needy persons to be fed
key_terms.شُهُودٌ: witnesses who establish the assessed value
key_terms.عَبْدًا خَطَأً: a slave killed unintentionally or by mistake
key_terms.قِيمَتُهُ: his monetary value owed as compensation
key_terms.يَمِينِهِ: his oath used in determining the valuation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone accidentally or intentionally kills a believing slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on compensation for killing a slave, distinguishing between accidental and intentional killing and setting an upper limit for the slave’s assessed value. It also explains how valuation is established through witnesses or oath, and in the case of intentionally killing a believing slave, it adds expiation and tawbah.
